claim_verdicts.evidence: Definition of the vocab term network-partition, stated exactly as outline item 1. Definitional; no behaviour, number or syntax. Consistent with etcd v3.6 failures page: "A network partition divides the etcd cluster into two parts".

Round 2: claim now also names A/C/P as in the section 3 bullet. Still no docs root in content/versions.yaml for the CAP theorem (grep for CAP/Gilbert/Brewer: 0 matches); etcd v3.6 failures page does not mention CAP. Cannot be checked against an allowed document.

Round 2: section 4 now reads "end the same way: every call to it fails, so the api must treat both as unreachable", which agrees with db-unreachable.sh @ stage-4 line 36: "(A real partition can also make calls hang; a stopped server fails fast.)" Both end in failed calls; the lesson no longer says they look the same.

"A networked system cannot rule partitions out" is presented as fact in section 4 ("'no partitions' is not an option you get to pick"). No allowed docs root states it in general; etcd v3.6 failures page treats network partition as one failure mode it handles, which is consistent but does not say partitions cannot be ruled out. Kind opinion; not blocking.

Script @ stage-4: lines 29-31 read product 3 and check EXISTS product:3; line 37 `docker compose stop db`; line 38 `trap restore EXIT`; restore() line 16 `docker compose start db`. Compose reference: "Stops running containers without removing them. They can be started again with `docker compose start`." (refs mirror is the compose v5 reference; command semantics unchanged for the pinned 2.33).

Round 2: version_key now npgsql; text matches the round 1 suggestion. Npgsql docs: Timeout "The time to wait (in seconds) while trying to establish a connection before terminating the attempt and generating an error." (default 15); Command Timeout default 30. So a call waits until a timeout, as the lesson now says. Script line 36 states the stopped server fails fast.

outputs/stage-4/scripts/backend/db-unreachable.txt: "GET /api/v1/products/3 (the copy in Redis) -> 200", "GET /api/v1/products (no copy, needs db) -> 500", "POST /api/v1/orders (must be saved in db) -> 500". The lesson's output block matches the file line for line.

OrderService.cs @ stage-4 line 50 `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();` then `return (order, Created: true);`. consistency-per-operation.md line 16: "Từ chối: đơn phải được lưu ở database của chủ" / "Đơn đã nhận phải còn". Round 2 added reasoning (customer told 'received', owner has no record) follows from that row; it is reasoning, not a new mechanism.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: text now says the copy expires 5 minutes after it was written. ProductCache.cs @ stage-4 line 18 `Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)`; line 90 `StringSetAsync(key, json, Ttl)` sets the TTL on write; line 41 reads PostgreSQL on a miss.

consistency-per-operation.md @ stage-4 line 13: "Trả lời bằng bản sao trong Redis nếu còn" / "Giá hiển thị cũ vài phút là chấp nhận được"; line 14: "Từ chối (lỗi)" / "Nghiệp vụ chấp nhận danh sách hơi cũ"; line 15 (search): "chưa có ở stage-4", "Từ chối (lỗi), như danh sách sản phẩm", "Cùng lựa chọn với danh sách sản phẩm"; line 16: "Đơn đã nhận phải còn".

Line 18: "Database lỗi: từ chối. Cổng lỗi: vẫn nhận, đơn ở `refunding`" / "Không bao giờ báo đã hoàn tiền trước khi cổng xác nhận". Section Hoàn tiền: "Không bước nào báo khách đã hoàn tiền khi cổng chưa xác nhận." 'like an order' matches line 16's refusal for the same database.
Line 17: "Xem đơn của mình ... Từ chối ... Khách vừa đặt đơn phải thấy ngay đơn đó".

Each 'fits when' is conditioned and its example matches a row of the repo table: product price (line 13, old price acceptable), saving an order (line 16, refuse), refunding (line 18, accepted, result later). Opinion with stated conditions, not opinion-as-fact.

Line 14 reason "Nghiệp vụ chấp nhận danh sách hơi cũ; đọc primary chỉ vì code chưa có bản sao nào khác"; line 53 "Chuyển một thao tác khác sang replica cần sửa bảng trên trước."; line 17 reason for order views. Recommendations carry conditions.

Round 2: lesson now says the data "still complies with the database's integrity rules, such as a foreign key pointing at an existing row, when the transaction commits". PostgreSQL 17 glossary, Consistency: "The property that the data in the database is always in compliance with integrity constraints." 'integrity rules' is a faithful paraphrase; a foreign key is an integrity constraint. CAP half: see claim 2.

Output file: product 3 -> 200, POST orders -> 500 with the same `db` stopped; the copy of product 3 was loaded from db (script lines 29-31, ProductCache line 41). consistency-per-operation.md lines 13 and 16 give the two rows different choices.

Same dependency as claims 2 and 4: no allowed docs root states that partitions cannot be switched off or that a cut-off part cannot answer and guarantee the latest value. Tried etcd v3.6 failures page (describes the minority side becoming unavailable - consistent, not a general statement). Kind opinion; not blocking.
